answer: Because the jetty solution is checked at the inlet gate and logged, the onyx audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 25 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. A farm of 123 pays that 87 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
